Why do introductions work? Path models for TBS and TDS

This document reproduces the path models in Sections 4.2 and 4.3 of the paper (Figures 5–9, Tables 6–7) and the robustness checks reported at the end of both sections. The regressions in Section 4.1 (Table 5) are in the document Effects of introductions on serendipity.

1 Setup

Code 
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(lavaan)
library(knitr)
library(DiagrammeR)
library(DiagrammeRsvg)
library(rsvg)

dir.create(here::here("figures"), showWarnings = FALSE)
Code 
data <- readr::read_csv(here::here("data", "long_df_scored.csv"))

1.1 Analysis subsets

As in the paper, the conditions are based on the song-level rating of se_1 (“The song differs from the type of music I normally listen to”). Songs rated 4 or higher form the outside-preference condition (taste-broadening serendipity, TBS); the remaining songs form the within-preference condition (taste-deepening serendipity, TDS).

Introduction type is dummy coded with no introduction as the reference category. The interaction terms are products of the regression factor scores computed in the data preparation document.

Code 
prepare_subset <- function(df) {
  df |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      intro_immersive    = as.integer(intro == "immersive_introduction"),
      intro_informative  = as.integer(intro == "informative_introduction"),
      inter_cope_complex = cp_reg * pc_a_reg,  # CP x PC (Section 4.2)
      inter_tr_pc        = tr_reg * pc_a_reg,  # TR x PC (Section 4.3, TBS)
      sess_id            = as.factor(sess_id)
    )
}

tbs_data <- data |> dplyr::filter(se_1 > 3) |> prepare_subset()
tds_data <- data |> dplyr::filter(se_1 < 4) |> prepare_subset()

stopifnot(
  "Outside-preference condition should contain 821 ratings" = nrow(tbs_data) == 821,
  "Within-preference condition should contain 535 ratings"  = nrow(tds_data) == 535
)

1.2 Helpers

All coefficients in the figures and tables are standardized (std.all); stars refer to the p-values of the corresponding unstandardized estimates (* p < .05, ** p < .01, *** p < .001). Every path that is shown is labeled in the model syntax, so the figures and tables are generated directly from the fitted models.

Code 
intro_labels <- c(
  no_introduction          = "No introduction",
  immersive_introduction   = "Immersive introduction",
  informative_introduction = "Informative introduction"
)

stars <- function(p) {
  dplyr::case_when(p < .001 ~ "***", p < .01 ~ "**", p < .05 ~ "*", TRUE ~ "")
}

# One labeled parameter (path, covariance, or defined effect) from a fitted model
param <- function(fit, label) {
  pe <- lavaan::parameterEstimates(fit, standardized = TRUE)
  row <- pe[pe$label == label, , drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(nrow(row) >= 1)
  row[1, ]
}

fmt_param <- function(fit, label, digits = 3) {
  r <- param(fit, label)
  paste0(formatC(r$std.all, format = "f", digits = digits), stars(r$pvalue))
}

# Fit indices as reported in the figure captions
fit_indices <- function(fit) {
  lavaan::fitMeasures(
    fit,
    c("cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr", "cfi.robust", "tli.robust", "rmsea.robust")
  ) |>
    round(3)
}

# DOT edge whose label and style follow the estimate
dot_edge <- function(fit, from, to, label, attrs = NULL, covariance = FALSE) {
  r <- param(fit, label)
  sig <- r$pvalue < .05
  style <- if (sig) {
    sprintf("style = solid, color = black, fontcolor = black, penwidth = %.1f",
            1 + 3 * abs(r$std.all))
  } else {
    "style = dashed, color = gray, fontcolor = gray, penwidth = 1"
  }
  if (covariance) style <- paste(style, "dir = both", sep = ", ")
  extra <- if (is.null(attrs)) "" else paste0(", ", attrs)
  sprintf("  %s -> %s [label = '%.2f%s', %s%s];",
          from, to, r$std.all, stars(r$pvalue), style, extra)
}

render_dot <- function(dot, file) {
  graph <- DiagrammeR::grViz(dot)
  graph |>
    DiagrammeRsvg::export_svg() |>
    charToRaw() |>
    rsvg::rsvg_pdf(here::here("figures", file))
  graph
}

# Pathway effects of the final serial models (Tables 6 and 7)
pathway_table <- function(fit, mediator, outcome) {
  pathways <- c(
    tr   = paste("Introduction -> Transportation ->", outcome),
    tr_m = paste("Introduction -> Transportation ->", mediator, "->", outcome),
    ce   = paste("Introduction -> Cognitive Elaboration ->", outcome),
    ce_m = paste("Introduction -> Cognitive Elaboration ->", mediator, "->", outcome)
  )
  purrr::imap_dfr(c(Immersive = "imm", Informative = "inf"), \(prefix, type) {
    tibble::tibble(
      `Introduction type` = type,
      Pathway = c(unname(pathways), paste("Total effect", type)),
      `Standardized effect` = purrr::map_chr(
        c(paste0(prefix, "_", names(pathways)), paste0("total_", prefix)),
        \(l) fmt_param(fit, l)
      )
    )
  })
}

# Fit the same model syntax with each serendipity operationalization
fit_operationalizations <- function(syntax_fn, outcomes, data, fit_fn) {
  purrr::map(rlang::set_names(outcomes), \(o) fit_fn(syntax_fn(o), data))
}

robustness_table <- function(fits, labels) {
  purrr::imap_dfr(fits, \(fit, outcome) {
    fi <- fit_indices(fit)
    tibble::tibble(
      Outcome = outcome,
      CFI = fi[["cfi"]], TLI = fi[["tli"]], RMSEA = fi[["rmsea"]], SRMR = fi[["srmr"]],
      !!!purrr::map(labels, \(l) fmt_param(fit, l))
    )
  })
}

2 Coping potential and perceived complexity (Section 4.2)

Following Silvia’s appraisal theory, the first pair of path models tests whether the effects of the introductions on TBS and TDS run through coping potential (CP), perceived complexity (PC), and their interaction. Both models include direct effects of the introductions on the outcome.

Code 
syntax_cp_pc <- function(outcome) {
  "
  # Measurement model
  coping_potential     =~ cp_1 + cp_2 + cp_3 + cp_5 + cp_6
  perceived_complexity =~ pc_4 + pc_5 + pc_6

  # Introductions -> appraisals
  coping_potential     ~ a1_imm * intro_immersive + a1_inf * intro_informative
  perceived_complexity ~ a2_imm * intro_immersive + a2_inf * intro_informative

  # Appraisals, their interaction, and direct effects -> outcome
  OUTCOME ~ b1 * coping_potential + b2 * perceived_complexity +
            b_int * inter_cope_complex +
            c_imm * intro_immersive + c_inf * intro_informative

  # Covariances
  coping_potential   ~~ cov_cp_pc * perceived_complexity
  inter_cope_complex ~~ cov_int_cp * coping_potential + cov_int_pc * perceived_complexity

  # Indirect effects (at the mean of the other appraisal)
  ind_imm_cp := a1_imm * b1
  ind_imm_pc := a2_imm * b2
  ind_inf_cp := a1_inf * b1
  ind_inf_pc := a2_inf * b2
  " |>
    stringr::str_replace_all("OUTCOME", outcome)
}

fit_cp_pc <- function(syntax, data) {
  lavaan::sem(model = syntax, data = data, cluster = "sess_id", estimator = "MLR")
}

fit_cp_pc_tbs <- fit_cp_pc(syntax_cp_pc("tbs"), tbs_data)
fit_cp_pc_tds <- fit_cp_pc(syntax_cp_pc("tds"), tds_data)

2.1 Descriptives: serendipity by CP and PC

Before the models, the crosstabs below show how often TBS and TDS occur at each combination of coping potential and perceived complexity (categorized regression factor scores).

Code 
cp_pc_crosstab <- function(df, outcome, title) {
  stopifnot(
    "pc_a_reg_cat and cp_reg_cat must be created in the data preparation document" =
      all(c("pc_a_reg_cat", "cp_reg_cat") %in% names(df))
  )
  levels_cat <- c("Low", "Average", "High")

  df |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(pc_a_reg_cat), !is.na(cp_reg_cat)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      pc_a_reg_cat = factor(pc_a_reg_cat, levels = levels_cat),
      cp_reg_cat   = factor(cp_reg_cat,   levels = levels_cat)
    ) |>
    dplyr::group_by(pc_a_reg_cat, cp_reg_cat) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      cell = sprintf("%.1f%% (n = %d)", 100 * mean(.data[[outcome]]), dplyr::n()),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = cp_reg_cat, values_from = cell) |>
    dplyr::rename(`PC \\ CP` = pc_a_reg_cat) |>
    knitr::kable(caption = title, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"))
}

Code 
dot_cp_pc <- function(fit, outcome_label) {
  paste(c(
    "digraph sem_model {",
    "  graph [layout = dot, rankdir = LR, splines = true, nodesep = 0.5, ranksep = 0.6]",
    "  node [shape = square, style = filled, fillcolor = '#F5F5F5', fontname = 'Helvetica', fontsize = 10, width = 1.2, fixedsize = false]",
    "  intro_imm [label = 'Immersive\\nIntro']; intro_inf [label = 'Informative\\nIntro'];",
    sprintf("  outcome [label = '%s'];", outcome_label),
    "  node [shape = circle, fillcolor = '#FFFFFF', width = 1.3]",
    "  cp [label = 'Coping\\nPotential']; pc [label = 'Perceived\\nComplexity'];",
    "  node [shape = diamond, style = filled, fillcolor = '#FFF3E0', height = 0.8]",
    "  inter [label = 'Interaction\\n(CP x PC)'];",
    "  { rank = same; intro_imm; intro_inf }",
    "  { rank = same; cp; pc }",
    dot_edge(fit, "intro_imm", "cp", "a1_imm"),
    dot_edge(fit, "intro_imm", "pc", "a2_imm"),
    dot_edge(fit, "intro_inf", "cp", "a1_inf"),
    dot_edge(fit, "intro_inf", "pc", "a2_inf"),
    "  cp -> inter [dir = none, color = gray50]; pc -> inter [dir = none, color = gray50];",
    dot_edge(fit, "cp", "outcome", "b1"),
    dot_edge(fit, "pc", "outcome", "b2"),
    dot_edge(fit, "inter", "outcome", "b_int"),
    dot_edge(fit, "intro_imm", "outcome", "c_imm", "constraint = false"),
    dot_edge(fit, "intro_inf", "outcome", "c_inf", "constraint = false"),
    dot_edge(fit, "cp", "pc", "cov_cp_pc", "constraint = false", covariance = TRUE),
    "}"
  ), collapse = "\n")
}

render_dot(dot_cp_pc(fit_cp_pc_tbs, "TBS"), "cp_pc_tbs.pdf")

For TDS, both introduction types keep substantial direct effects, so coping potential and perceived complexity account for only a small part of their effect.

2.4 Ceiling effect (Figure 7)

Songs within the listener’s typical preferences already score high on coping potential and perceived complexity without an introduction, leaving little room for the introductions to raise these appraisals.

Code 
intro_colors <- c(
  "No introduction"          = "#D3D3D3",
  "Immersive introduction"   = "#87CEEB",
  "Informative introduction" = "#F8AD9D"
)

dens_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  "Outside-preference" = tbs_data,
  "Within-preference"  = tds_data,
  .id = "condition"
) |>
  dplyr::select(condition, intro, cp_reg, pc_a_reg) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(cp_reg, pc_a_reg), names_to = "variable", values_to = "score") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    variable = dplyr::recode(variable, cp_reg = "Coping Potential", pc_a_reg = "Perceived Complexity"),
    intro    = factor(intro_labels[intro], levels = intro_labels)
  )

p_ceiling <- ggplot(dens_data, aes(x = score, fill = intro, color = intro)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_grid(condition ~ variable, scales = "free") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = intro_colors) +
  scale_color_manual(values = intro_colors) +
  labs(x = "Regression Factor Scores", y = "Density",
       fill = "Introduction Type", color = "Introduction Type") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

ggsave(here::here("figures", "ceiling.pdf"), p_ceiling, width = 9, height = 6)
p_ceiling

2.5 Robustness checks

The models are re-estimated with the stricter operationalizations from the data preparation document: without se_5 in the fortuitous criterion (_fort_strict) and, for TDS, additionally without the uncovering criterion (tds_no_uncover).

Code

  syntax_cp_pc, c("tbs", "tbs_fort_strict"), tbs_data, fit_cp_pc
)
rob_cp_pc_tds <- fit_operationalizations(
  syntax_cp_pc, c("tds", "tds_fort_strict", "tds_no_uncover"), tds_data, fit_cp_pc
)

3 Transportation and cognitive elaboration (Section 4.3)

3.1 Model selection

The full serial models add transportation (TR) and cognitive elaboration (CE) as first-stage mediators of coping potential and perceived complexity.

Code 
full_syntax <- function(outcome, direct_effects) {
  paste0("
  transportation        =~ tr_1 + tr_2 + tr_3 + tr_4
  cognitive_elaboration =~ ce_1 + ce_3 + ce_4
  coping_potential      =~ cp_1 + cp_2 + cp_3 + cp_5 + cp_6
  perceived_complexity  =~ pc_4 + pc_5 + pc_6

  transportation        ~ intro_immersive + intro_informative
  cognitive_elaboration ~ intro_immersive + intro_informative
  coping_potential      ~ transportation + cognitive_elaboration + intro_immersive + intro_informative
  perceived_complexity  ~ transportation + cognitive_elaboration + intro_immersive + intro_informative

  ", outcome, " ~ b_cp * coping_potential + b_pc * perceived_complexity +
      b_tr * transportation + b_ce * cognitive_elaboration + b_int * inter_cope_complex",
    if (direct_effects) " + intro_immersive + intro_informative" else "", "

  transportation     ~~ cognitive_elaboration
  coping_potential   ~~ perceived_complexity
  inter_cope_complex ~~ coping_potential + perceived_complexity
  ")
}

fit_mlr <- function(syntax, data) {
  lavaan::sem(
    model = syntax, data = data,
    estimator = "MLR", se = "robust", cluster = "sess_id", missing = "fiml"
  )
}

# TBS: no direct effects, since Section 4.2 showed full mediation
fit_full_tbs <- fit_mlr(full_syntax("tbs", direct_effects = FALSE), tbs_data)
# TDS: direct effects retained, since Section 4.2 showed partial mediation
fit_full_tds <- fit_mlr(full_syntax("tds", direct_effects = TRUE), tds_data)

full_labels <- c(
  "TR -> outcome" = "b_tr", "CE -> outcome" = "b_ce",
  "CP -> outcome" = "b_cp", "PC -> outcome" = "b_pc", "CP x PC -> outcome" = "b_int"
)

dplyr::bind_rows(
  TBS = purrr::map(full_labels, \(l) fmt_param(fit_full_tbs, l)) |> tibble::as_tibble(),
  TDS = purrr::map(full_labels, \(l) fmt_param(fit_full_tds, l)) |> tibble::as_tibble(),
  .id = "Model"
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Effects on the outcome in the full serial models")
Effects on the outcome in the full serial models
Model TR -> outcome CE -> outcome CP -> outcome PC -> outcome CP x PC -> outcome
TBS 0.469*** 0.107** -0.022 0.230*** 0.069*
TDS 0.288*** 0.447*** -0.119* 0.060 -0.015

For TBS, coping potential no longer predicts the outcome once transportation is included, so coping potential is dropped. Its interaction with perceived complexity is replaced by the interaction between transportation and perceived complexity. For TDS, perceived complexity and the CP x PC interaction do not predict the outcome, so both are dropped.

In the final TBS model, the interaction term is allowed to covary with transportation and perceived complexity. Transportation and perceived complexity themselves are linked through the regression path TR → PC, so no additional covariance between them is estimated.

3.2 Final models

Code 
syntax_final_tbs <- function(outcome) {
  "
  transportation        =~ tr_1 + tr_2 + tr_3 + tr_4
  cognitive_elaboration =~ ce_1 + ce_3 + ce_4
  perceived_complexity  =~ pc_4 + pc_5 + pc_6

  transportation        ~ a1_imm * intro_immersive + a1_inf * intro_informative
  cognitive_elaboration ~ a2_imm * intro_immersive + a2_inf * intro_informative
  perceived_complexity  ~ d1 * transportation + d2 * cognitive_elaboration

  OUTCOME ~ b1 * transportation + b2 * perceived_complexity +
            b3 * inter_tr_pc + b4 * cognitive_elaboration

  transportation       ~~ cov_tr_ce * cognitive_elaboration
  transportation       ~~ cov_tr_int * inter_tr_pc
  perceived_complexity ~~ cov_pc_int * inter_tr_pc

  imm_tr    := a1_imm * b1
  imm_tr_m  := a1_imm * d1 * b2
  imm_ce    := a2_imm * b4
  imm_ce_m  := a2_imm * d2 * b2
  total_imm := imm_tr + imm_tr_m + imm_ce + imm_ce_m

  inf_tr    := a1_inf * b1
  inf_tr_m  := a1_inf * d1 * b2
  inf_ce    := a2_inf * b4
  inf_ce_m  := a2_inf * d2 * b2
  total_inf := inf_tr + inf_tr_m + inf_ce + inf_ce_m
  " |>
    stringr::str_replace_all("OUTCOME", outcome)
}

syntax_final_tds <- function(outcome) {
  "
  transportation        =~ tr_1 + tr_2 + tr_3 + tr_4
  cognitive_elaboration =~ ce_1 + ce_3 + ce_4
  coping_potential      =~ cp_1 + cp_2 + cp_3 + cp_5 + cp_6

  transportation        ~ a1_imm * intro_immersive + a1_inf * intro_informative
  cognitive_elaboration ~ a2_imm * intro_immersive + a2_inf * intro_informative
  coping_potential      ~ d1 * transportation + d2 * cognitive_elaboration

  OUTCOME ~ b1 * transportation + b2 * coping_potential + b4 * cognitive_elaboration

  transportation ~~ cov_tr_ce * cognitive_elaboration

  imm_tr    := a1_imm * b1
  imm_tr_m  := a1_imm * d1 * b2
  imm_ce    := a2_imm * b4
  imm_ce_m  := a2_imm * d2 * b2
  total_imm := imm_tr + imm_tr_m + imm_ce + imm_ce_m

  inf_tr    := a1_inf * b1
  inf_tr_m  := a1_inf * d1 * b2
  inf_ce    := a2_inf * b4
  inf_ce_m  := a2_inf * d2 * b2
  total_inf := inf_tr + inf_tr_m + inf_ce + inf_ce_m
  " |>
    stringr::str_replace_all("OUTCOME", outcome)
}

fit_final_tbs <- fit_mlr(syntax_final_tbs("tbs"), tbs_data)
fit_final_tds <- fit_mlr(syntax_final_tds("tds"), tds_data)

dot_final_tbs <- paste(c(
  "digraph sem_tbs {",

  "  trans [label = 'Transportation']; cogelab [label = 'Cognitive\\nElaboration'];",
  "  node [shape = circle, fillcolor = '#FFFFFF', width = 1.2]",
  "  pc [label = 'Perceived\\nComplexity'];",
  "  node [shape = diamond, style = filled, fillcolor = '#FFF3E0', height = 0.9, width = 1.3]",
  "  inter [label = 'Interaction\\n(Trans x PC)'];",
  "  node [shape = square, style = filled, fillcolor = '#F5F5F5', width = 1.2]",
  "  tbs [label = 'TBS'];",

  dot_edge(fit_final_tbs, "inter", "tbs", "b3"),
  dot_edge(fit_final_tbs, "pc", "tbs", "b2"),

  "}"
), collapse = "\n")
